ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-028", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Alert: auth-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 07:42 UTC)
Alerting service: auth
Alert time: 2026-03-05T07:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-03-05T06:00:00Z to 2026-03-05T09:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-05T08:30:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-05T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate evolution for auth service)
  Result: M-005: Change detected at 2026-03-05T07:20:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 30.32 after (564.2 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-005] auth.error_rate_pct from 2026-03-05T07:00:00Z to 2026-03-05T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.22 max=41.32 mean=24.01 last=41.07; mean=24.01. Change detected at 2026-03-05T07:20:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 30.32 after (564.2 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-05T07:20:00Z = 0.26 (first point after the change); 2026-03-05T07:30:00Z = 0.22 (lowest); 2026-03-05T07:50:00Z = 41.32 (peak); 2026-03-05T08:30:00Z = 41.07 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-05T08:30:00Z", "metric": "restarts", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-05T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if auth service experienced restarts around the alert time)
  Result: M-009: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-009] auth.restarts from 2026-03-05T07:00:00Z to 2026-03-05T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=0 mean=0 last=0; mean=0. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-03-05T07:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-03-05T07:00:00Z = 0 (peak); 2026-03-05T08:30:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-03-05T07:45:00Z", "query": "deploy,config,cert,error,warn,fail", "service": "auth", "start": "2026-03-05T07:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search auth logs for events or errors leading up to the alert)
  Result: 5 matching log lines.
  [L-0283] 2026-03-05T07:40:05Z auth ERROR SSL handshake failed: certificate has expired notAfter=2026-03-05T07:39:00Z subject=CN=auth.internal.shop
  [L-0285] 2026-03-05T07:40:31Z auth ERROR x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-03-05T07:40:05Z is after 2026-03-05T07:39:00Z
  [L-0289] 2026-03-05T07:40:55Z auth WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0291] 2026-03-05T07:41:14Z auth INFO config heartbeat ok revision=813
  [L-0300] 2026-03-05T07:43:34Z auth WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
Step 4: runbook_retrieve {"query": "How to handle an expired TLS certificate or renew certificate for a service"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance and mitigation steps for expired TLS certificate incidents.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-07-7 (similarity 0.73).
  [R-07-7] Expired TLS certificate - Escalation (similarity 0.73): Call the security team if the issuing authority cannot be reached or there is any sign that private keys were exposed. Tell the service owner so renewal automation can be fixed.
  [R-07-5] Expired TLS certificate - Mitigation (similarity 0.72): Issue and install a renewed certificate, then reload or restart the service so it picks the new one up. If automated renewal failed, fix whatever blocked it and run the renewal by hand. Check other certificates issued around the same day for the same fault.
  [R-07-1] Expired TLS certificate - Summary (similarity 0.68): A service certificate passed its expiry date, so clients can no longer complete secure handshakes with it. Nothing about the application itself is wrong, which makes this easy to miss when looking only at the code and its recent changes.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- expired_tls_cert: Auth service logs explicitly indicate that SSL handshakes are failing because the internal TLS certificate expired at 07:39:00 UTC, and runbook guidance confirms the symptoms and mitigation steps. (evidence: L-0283, L-0285, R-07-7, R-07-5)
